abstract_sentences.text: Prediction algorithms are increasingly used to inform decisions about humans, but maximizing accuracy—the standard learning objective—is not necessarily optimal for this purpose.
Instead, we propose optimizing social welfare, defined as the average gain users receive from correct predictions.
Welfare enables to express, and therefore account for, heterogeneity in how much users benefit from accuracy.

evidence.anchor: heterogeneity in how much users benefit

abstract_sentences.text: But since these valuations are private and users can benefit from overreporting them, learning must simultaneously elicit truthful values and optimize welfare with respect to them.
To this end, we propose a novel learning algorithm that incorporates a truthful auction.
We show how to compute allocations and prices efficiently, and bound the number of paying users—which surprisingly is independent of the sample size.
We conclude with experiments on real and synthetic data that demonstrate our algorithm and explore the connections between welfare and accuracy.

evidence.anchor: The social domain has much to gain

final_judgment.single_storyline: Treat accuracy as scarce allocation, use a truthful auction to elicit private benefit values as classifier weights, then use stability to explain a small train-time payment burden.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main body keeps the setup, welfare/auction mechanism, informal theory, Algorithm 1, Table 1, Figures 1–3, discussion and deployment-facing impact boundary.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix A gives formal proofs and conditions, B gives payment pseudocode, C gives data/model details, and D gives payment, loss, value-variance and k-NN extensions.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 establishes bids-to-allocation-to-payments; Figure 2 turns the theorem into simple scaling plots; Figure 3 connects the mechanism to welfare tradeoffs on semi-synthetic data.
final_judgment.largest_gap: No human/deployment evidence for rational bidding or who bears payments; WKHP feature exclusion is internally inconsistent; experimental uncertainty reporting is sparse.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Keep the mechanism, theorem statement, decisive visual evidence and deployment boundary in the main body; place derivations and parameter sweeps in an explicitly called appendix.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The appendix call must still state conditions and data construction clearly when they determine whether the headline claim applies; fixed-lambda scope and the WKHP conflict show the limit here.
